subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

rungs.aha: Distance records how much path was travelled, while displacement records the signed change from start to finish; a long trip can have zero displacement.
learner_owns: Can trace an object's route from a start point to an end point.
must_contain: A marked one-dimensional axis with a declared positive direction.
An out-and-back path where path length is nonzero but the finish is at the start.

misconception.wrong_idea: Distance travelled and displacement are always the same number.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Walk 5 m east and 5 m west back to the start. What is the distance travelled, and what change in position remains?
misconception.repair: Trace the path for distance; compare only the final and initial positions for displacement, including direction.

rungs.closure: Given a one-dimensional route, report both total distance and signed displacement and explain why they can differ.

controlled_variation.vary: how far the traveller goes before returning to the start
controlled_variation.hold: the same start and finish point
controlled_variation.notice: distance changes while displacement remains zero

controlled_variation.vary: the finish point on the marked axis
controlled_variation.notice: equal distances can end with different signed displacements

rungs.aha: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, while average velocity uses displacement over the same time; neither is found by averaging listed speeds unless the time weighting makes that valid.
learner_owns: Distance records how much path was travelled, while displacement records the signed change from start to finish; a long trip can have zero displacement.
must_contain: A round trip with unequal speeds on equal-distance legs.
The total-distance-over-total-time construction written before any averaging shortcut.

misconception.wrong_idea: For a trip with two speeds, average speed is always the arithmetic mean of those speeds.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A vehicle covers equal distances at 60 km/h and 30 km/h. Is its average speed 45 km/h? Which leg takes longer?
misconception.repair: Compute each leg's time, add total distance and total time, then divide; use displacement instead of distance only for average velocity.

rungs.closure: For a two-leg trip, calculate average speed from totals and separately state average velocity when the final position is known.

controlled_variation.hold: equal distance on both legs and the faster leg's speed
controlled_variation.notice: the slower leg occupies more of the total time and pulls the average speed toward it

rungs.aha: Velocity and acceleration are different statements: velocity can be zero at an instant while acceleration remains nonzero and fixes how velocity changes next.
learner_owns: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, while average velocity uses displacement over the same time; neither is found by averaging listed speeds unless the time weighting makes that valid.
must_contain: A velocity-time plot crossing zero with a nonzero slope.
The instant at the top of a vertical trip distinguished from an interval of rest.

misconception.wrong_idea: If velocity is zero at an instant, acceleration must also be zero at that instant.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: At the highest point of a vertically thrown ball, the velocity is momentarily zero. Is the next moment also at the same velocity?
misconception.repair: Ask what velocity does immediately before and after the instant: a sign change in velocity requires nonzero acceleration even when the instantaneous velocity is zero.

rungs.closure: Read a turning point from a motion description or velocity-time graph and state velocity and acceleration separately.

controlled_variation.vary: the instant from just before to just after the top of the motion
controlled_variation.notice: velocity passes through zero and changes sign while acceleration keeps the same direction
the time of the zero-velocity instant changes but the acceleration at that instant does not

rungs.aha: The constant-acceleration equations are a model with a condition: they apply only when acceleration stays constant over the interval.
learner_owns: Velocity and acceleration are different statements: velocity can be zero at an instant while acceleration remains nonzero and fixes how velocity changes next.
must_contain: Two velocity-time plots over equal intervals, one straight and one curved.
A check of whether acceleration is constant before any constant-acceleration equation is selected.

misconception.wrong_idea: The familiar kinematic equations can be used whenever initial velocity, time and some acceleration value are given.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A velocity-time graph curves upward. Can one constant acceleration value describe the whole interval well enough to use v = u + at exactly?
misconception.repair: Test the model condition first: constant acceleration gives a straight velocity-time graph and one unchanged acceleration value over the interval.

rungs.closure: Given several motion descriptions or graphs, classify which intervals permit exact use of the constant-acceleration equations and justify each classification.

controlled_variation.vary: the time interval chosen on a straight velocity-time graph
controlled_variation.notice: the same acceleration describes every sub-interval

controlled_variation.vary: the graph from straight to curved
controlled_variation.hold: the same starting velocity and total duration
controlled_variation.notice: one acceleration value no longer describes every part of the motion

family.invariant_demand: Declare the positive direction and time interval, distinguish path quantities from signed change, choose a relation whose assumptions fit the motion, and keep velocity and acceleration as separate quantities.
family.difficult_move: Deciding from the words or graph which signed quantity and which motion model are actually being asked for before substituting numbers.
family.independent_check: The sign must match the declared axis, units must match the requested quantity, and any constant-acceleration calculation must agree with the slope/shape of the velocity-time representation.

support_ladder.handed_over: The positive direction, time interval, and the relevant motion representation are labelled.
The positive direction and time interval are labelled.
Only the story, table, path, or graph is supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A velocity-time graph must be translated into signed displacement and acceleration statements without a verbal motion story.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which graph features correspond to signed change and to acceleration

transfer.changed_demand: A motion interval has changing acceleration and the learner must decide that constant-acceleration equations are not an exact model.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether acceleration is constant over the interval

transfer.changed_demand: A journey reverses direction in several stages, requiring segment-by-segment distance, displacement, and elapsed-time accounting.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which segment signs contribute to displacement but not to distance
